prize_parts.citation: For the development of general, ligand-controlled palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling reactions
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I keep the round-1 configuration: B003 (Buchwald, Hartwig) and B024 (Liu alone), three people in all. B003 is the clearest case on the shortlist of a general method that changed what chemists do routinely. Mechanism-guided ligand design (bulky, electron-rich phosphines and later biaryl phosphines) turned aryl amination from a narrow, harsh reaction into a predictable one that is used daily in drug discovery, process chemistry and materials synthesis. Attribution is clean, the two groups developed the general methods in parallel, and thirty years of independent use leave no maturity doubt. For B024, reading the full round-1 exchange I now see the chemical step more clearly than in my opening: the adenine base editor required a deaminase that acts on DNA, which no natural enzyme does, so TadA had to be evolved for that substrate. That is a new nucleobase transformation made programmable, not just a delivery of an old reaction, and the double-strand-break-free outcome is the decisive practical difference from 2020. I keep Liu alone because he is the conceptual and directing author of both editor families and because three seats is the hard limit once B003 takes two. In answer to the chair, the discovery step I would put in the citation for B003 is ligand-controlled catalytic C-N bond formation, and for B024 it is the programmable conversion of a defined base without cleaving both strands.
statement.case_against: Against B003: the 2010 prize for Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling covers C-C bond formation, and some colleagues will see C-N coupling as an extension; Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is a genuine precursor that a careful citation must acknowledge. Against B024 as I credit it: Komor and Gaudelli wrote the decisive papers, and a Liu-only credit risks reading as a demotion of the people who did the bench work. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) also have a priority claim that I cannot settle from the shortlist, and a citation naming only the capability does not resolve it. Against the pairing: a classical synthetic method plus a genome-engineering tool shares no obvious theme beyond programmable or predictable control of bond formation, and this is a weakness that Linke's chair questions fairly press. If the committee judges that Liu alone is indefensible, I would withdraw B024 from my configuration and propose B003 alone, because I would not support a trio credit that pushes B003 out of a prize that is already limited to three names.

responses.point: Linke accepts that Buchwald-Hartwig coupling is mature and widely used but asks whether C-N coupling is a distinct discovery from the 2010 cross-coupling prize or an extension of it, and holds B003 as an alternative.
responses.response: I take the question seriously and answer it on chemistry. The 2010 prize recognised Pd-catalysed C-C coupling via organometallic nucleophiles, where transmetalation and reductive elimination to carbon are comparatively easy. C-N coupling failed for a different reason: amine binding, deprotonation and C-N reductive elimination from palladium are hard, and beta-hydride elimination competes. It needed ligand classes that were designed for those steps, so the advance is a distinct mechanistic solution, not a larger substrate table. That is the same distinction that separated the Suzuki and Negishi chemistry from Heck chemistry in 2010. I agree the Kosugi precursor should be named in the discussion, but it was a toxic tin-amide reaction of narrow scope. I would not accept your point that maturity alone cannot lift B003 above the top two, because the other criteria here, clean attribution and demonstrated use, are met by it and by few others.

responses.point: Brzezinski answers my chemistry-versus-biology objection to PROTACs by saying that the rational design of a heterobifunctional small molecule and its ternary-complex energetics is chemistry acting on a biological pathway, and that B003 looks incremental after 2010.
responses.response: This is a fair point and it shifts me partly. The ternary-complex cooperativity work, where linker and surface complementarity decide degradation efficiency, is real physical-organic chemistry, and I accept that I understated it in round 1. It does not remove my other two reservations: no PROTAC is an approved drug, and the credit divides into the PROTAC lineage and the cereblon glue lineage, so a three-name cut does not honour both. I therefore still hold B009 as an alternative, not as a part of the prize. On the 2010 overlap I have answered Heiner above; I would add that you ranked B003 third and listed it as your first alternative, so we agree on the merit and differ only on novelty, and I would ask you to weigh the ligand-design argument.

responses.point: Chabes argues that adenine base editing is the strongest evidence of real chemistry because no natural DNA adenine deaminase existed and TadA had to be evolved, and he proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as the whole prize.
responses.response: Your adenine editor argument is the best one made in round 1 for treating B024 as chemistry, and I have taken it into my own case above. I disagree with the consequence you draw for names. If B024 stands alone with a trio I would find that a defensible prize, but it would lose the B003 part, and B003 is the stronger chemistry on its own. I also think the committee should be honest that Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experiments, which is why my Liu-alone credit is a concession to the three-person limit and not a judgement of merit. I am open to a Liu-Komor-Gaudelli single-part prize being on the final ballot, but I would still rank B003 plus Liu above it.

responses.point: Aqvist pairs base editing with PROTACs as two designed chemical capabilities with large generative potential, and says he would shift the degradation credit to Handa if the cereblon glue lineage is the mature core.
responses.response: I agree with Johan that Liu alone is a clean B024 credit and that the double-strand-break-free chemistry is distinct from 2020. I do not follow the argument that a PROTAC part fits as the second part. Your own caveat shows the problem: if the credit might move from Crews and Deshaies to Handa, the discovery is not yet settled enough for a citation, and I would rather wait a year than award the wrong lineage. My proposal covers the same three-person arithmetic with Buchwald and Hartwig, whose attribution has no such open question.

responses.point: Zou proposes dye-sensitized solar cells (Gratzel, O'Regan) with clean attribution and thirty years of confirmation, while naming that the technology has been superseded by perovskites.
responses.response: I recognise the attribution and maturity arguments, and they are as strong as for B003. My hesitation is still the lasting impact: the lineage into perovskites is real, but the prize would then raise the question of whether the perovskite part, with six candidate names, should be considered at the same time, and I cannot resolve that with a three-person cap. I do not move to B025, and would keep it off my ballot, but I would back a materials prize in a later year when the dye and perovskite histories can be credited in sequence.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that C-N coupling is distinct from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize, and whether the Kosugi precursor is treated as a priority issue.
Whether a Liu-only credit in B024 is defensible, given that Komor and Gaudelli wrote the two foundational papers and the Target-AID priority record is unresolved.
Whether a classical synthetic method paired with a genome-engineering tool reads as a coherent prize or as two unrelated parts.
How the committee weighs the 2020 CRISPR prize against base editing as a follow-on, which I now regard as a lesser objection than the one in my opening.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal to disclose. I am a synthetic organic chemist at Lund with no recorded collaboration, institutional tie or financial link to Buchwald, Hartwig, Liu or any other credited name on the shortlist. Linke and Sparr are Lund colleagues, but none of the shortlisted candidates is tied to Lund in the supplied materials. My disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
